article.headline: GTA 6 storms bring hurricanes, wind ripples, and 170 animal species to Florida
article.summary: Rockstar Games confirmed Grand Theft Auto 6 features an advanced weather system with hurricanes, tropical storms, and dynamic environmental details across over 170 animal species in its recreation of Florida.
article.body:
Rockstar's version of Miami will be battered by hurricanes and tropical storms that transform the environment with stunning visual detail. According to Owen Shepherd, vice president of art for lighting and rendering at Rockstar Games, these storms bring "heavy clouds, strong winds, dense atmospherics, and a lot of rain" so that "everything is dripping wet, water is gushing off roof edges and lampposts, thunder rumbles, and flashes of lightning light up the clouds dramatically."

The weather system matters because it reflects Rockstar's push to make GTA 6 feel like a living, breathing world. The company has redesigned its entire weather engine to be more localized and persistent, altering how players interact with the map during different conditions.

Beyond the major storms, Rockstar engineered subtle atmospheric effects throughout the game. "Offshore breezes after sunset, convectional updrafts, and occlusion from buildings" will create realistic wind patterns, Shepherd explained. "Hair and debris will swirl around on rooftops; gusts of wind will blow ripples over the water surface and bend the grass in swamps." The dynamic cloudscapes shift from clear Miami winter skies to the towering cumulonimbus clouds of Floridian summer afternoons. Rockstar also populated its Florida with over 170 animal species that players can encounter. The company has not yet detailed how hurricanes and tropical storms will mechanically impact gameplay, though the system is described as persistent and designed to alter the environment significantly.

article.headline: Tom Cruise transforms into paunchy oil baron for Iñárritu's weirdest satire yet
article.summary: Tom Cruise plays an aging Texan oil tycoon in Digger, director Alejandro G Iñárritu's bizarre eco-satire about irresponsible drilling that triggers a global crisis.
article.body:
Tom Cruise is unrecognizable under prosthetic makeup as Digger Rockwell, a balding, greying, paunchy oil baron who bears little resemblance to the ageless action hero audiences know. The transformation is so extreme that it marks the biggest risk of his career—not a stunt injury, but the risk of being called pretentious and self-indulgent, or of being associated with a potential flop.

Director Alejandro G Iñárritu, who made Birdman and The Revenant, has created what BBC calls the "weirdest film" Cruise has ever made. The satirical comedy is a divisive, conceptually challenging eco-satire that is unlikely to be mistaken for Mission: Impossible. Most viewers won't go to see it, and some who do may walk out halfway through. The Guardian calls it "the most disappointing film of the year," while BBC gives it four stars, praising high-concept twists beneath the bizarre surface.

The plot centers on Rockwell's irresponsible drilling practices in the Arctic. When his chief scientist Ganesh warns him that a vast ice floe—many times the size of Manhattan—has broken away and is moving toward Norway's coast with the force of a nuclear attack, Rockwell remains aggressively unrepentant. He crashes a White House crisis meeting with the President to make his case. Cruise even appears in underwear as a cheeky homage to his breakthrough film Risky Business, while his character's mansion is decorated with more stuffed exotic animals than a Victorian museum—despite his deep worry over his scrawny pet cat.

article.headline: Ted Lasso season 4 episode 9 honors late actor Anthony Head with tribute card
article.summary: Apple TV's Ted Lasso included a tribute card for actor Anthony Head in Season 4, Episode 9 following his death in June 2026 at age 72.
article.body:
Ted Lasso paid respects to Anthony Head, who died in June 2026 at age 72 from complications due to pneumonia. The Apple TV comedy series featured a tribute card before the end credits of Season 4, Episode 9, titled "Mae Rides the Bus."

Head played Rupert Manion, the former owner of AFC Richmond and ex-husband of Rebecca Welton, across 18 episodes in the series' first three seasons. His family released a statement saying he "passed away peacefully of complications due to pneumonia, surrounded by his family." They added: "It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed firsthand the impact both he and his work have had on so many."

Cast members shared their condolences publicly. Brett Goldstein called Head "a brilliant actor" and "the best person," describing him as "infinitely charming and kind and fun and a joy." Hannah Waddingham reflected on his influence on her performance: "There is no Rebecca without Rupert. He undoubtedly made my Rebecca what she was. He was one of the finest gentlemen I've ever met." Jeremy Swift posted: "Goodbye Tony, we adored you, Rest in Peace my friend." Actress Annette Badland remembered him as "funny, bright, inclusive, generous" with "wry humor" and "a very beautiful man."

article.headline: India opts to bowl in second ODI as West Indies seek first series win since 2006
article.summary: India won the coin toss and chose to bowl first against West Indies in the second ODI on Wednesday in Guwahati, with India leading the three-match series after an eight-wicket victory on Sunday.
article.body:
India handed pace bowler Auqib Nabi his ODI debut in the second match, replacing allrounder Nitish Reddy to strengthen the bowling attack. West Indies made four changes, bringing in allrounder Sherfane Rutherford, allrounder Keemo Paul, and left-arm wrist spinner Vitel Lawes, while opener Justin Greaves was ruled out due to a calf injury and replaced by Keacy Carty.

The West Indies have not won a bilateral ODI series against India in 18 years, with their last victory coming in 2006 by a 4-1 margin at home. Since then, India have won all 12 bilateral series between the sides. According to West Indies captain Shai Hope, his team views this challenge as an opportunity to test themselves against the best. "Playing anyone in their home conditions will always be challenging," Hope said, but emphasized the importance of adapting to subcontinental conditions.

The pitch at Barsapara Cricket Stadium has more grass than the first venue, typically favoring spinners, though batters are expected to find scoring relatively straightforward during the day. India leads the three-match series 1-0 following Sunday's eight-wicket triumph in Thiruvananthapuram. The West Indies are ranked 10th in the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings and cannot secure automatic qualification for the 2027 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup after the second ODI concludes.

article.headline: Iran reviews US ceasefire proposal as attacks hit Strait of Hormuz tankers
article.summary: Iran's leadership is reviewing a U.S. counterproposal for a seven-day ceasefire, while three commercial vessels including an oil tanker were hit by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday.
article.body:
Three commercial vessels, including an oil tanker and a liquefied natural gas tanker, were struck by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran reviewed the latest U.S. proposal aimed at ending the conflict. The timing underscored the high stakes for global energy markets, as the waterway previously carried roughly one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas.

Iran has demanded sanctions relief for its oil sector, the release of frozen assets, an end to the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports, and a seven-day ceasefire across the region. The U.S. counterproposal calls for a seven-day ceasefire, though it remains unclear whether Washington has accepted Iran's broader conditions tied to reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented the U.S. proposal to President Masoud Pezeshkian during a Cabinet meeting on Wednesday.

Iran has maintained a blockade on commercial shipping through the strategic waterway since the conflict began in late February, while the U.S. has sought to restrict Iran's oil exports through a counterblockade of its ports. Qatari mediators have been shuttling messages between the sides, though negotiations have made limited progress as the two countries remain divided over key concessions. The counterproposal follows talks in New York last week involving Araghchi and U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
